text:
ana: Heads up — want to run a controlled loadtest tomorrow to validate admission controller/backpressure in us-west1 GPU pool. Goal: confirm queueing thresholds, rejection behavior, and fallback routing to cpu-fallback-pool. Running synthetic mix of short chat + long-stream tokens. Who can help scope and run?

mike: I can own infra side. Need traffic profile + safe rollback plan. Recommend a 3-stage ramp: soak, spike, sustained. Keep burst windows < 10m.

jin: Add me for metrics collection. I'll wire up dashboards for gpu_queue_length, admission_reject_rate, token_latency_p95, model_load_failures. Also want to capture per-model admission counters.

ana: @ana did you mean cpu-fallback-pool as pre-warmed? we should avoid cold starts for safety.

ana: (sorry typo, meant sara)

ana: sara: we have a pre-warmed small batch in us-west1 for Llama2-13B. Should be fine. Need to ensure fallback model versions are compatible.

mike: Test plan draft:
- stage 1 (soak, 30m): 200 rps mixed short prompts (avg 20 tokens) across 3 models to verify steady-state queueing
- stage 2 (spike, 5m): ramp to 2k rps to force admission kicks, observe reject vs queue growth
- stage 3 (sustain, 20m): maintain 800 rps to validate auto-throttle and routing to cpu-fallback

Use `loadgen` with this YAML: 
```yaml
profile: mixed-chat
ramp: [60s, 5m, 30s]
mix:
  - model: rlx-llama2-13b
    weight: 50
  - model: rlx-llama2-70b-q4
    weight: 30
  - model: rlx-small-2.7b
    weight: 20
requests_per_call: 1
prompt_tokens: {short: 1-40, long: 200-1200}
```

mike: We'll run from infra-loadgen-usw1 with isolated tenancy and tagged test-id=backpress-2303. Kill-switch: `pkill loadgen` + API toggle to open admission.

jin: For dashboards, I'll add alert thresholds: admission_reject_rate > 1% -> paging, gpu_queue_length > 500 -> warn, token_latency_p95 > 2s -> warn. Also will capture admission controller logs: `admission.*` with sampling 1:10.

ana: cost check — rough estimate: peak 2k rps for 5m across mixed models ~ estimated 40 GPU-minutes + fallback CPU. Budget OK but flagging to finance for record.

mike: One caveat: network egress limits in the region may affect long-stream tests; recommend limiting long-stream ratio to 10% during spike.

jin: Good call. I'll add sampling for long-stream only + track net_bandwidth_per_node metric.

sara: Also ensure we don't run on nodes marked for HW maintenance. I'll patch node-selector to avoid maintenance pool.

capacity-bot: [auto] current reserved GPU headroom in us-west1: 22% (estimated for next 6h) — running test may cause autoscaler to allocate burst nodes; expect ~2m provisioning time.

ana: If autoscaler needs to spin new nodes during spike, we should treat that as part of test — we want to observe admission behavior during provisioning lag.

mike: Agreed. We'll keep autoscaler on. Plan to run test at 2026-03-19 02:00 UTC to hit low-prod window. Who signs off?

ana: I sign off. I will notify customer-facing teams and set floor to pause if any prod anomaly.

jin: I sign off for metrics.

sara: Sign off for node scheduling, will ensure maintenance excluded.

mike: I'll execute. Posting run log afterwards + tl;dr with key numbers (peak queue length, rejection %, fallback % by model, latency p95).

ana: Great. After test let's iterate on admission thresholds: consider moving queue_threshold from 400 -> 300 if we see high p95 tail.

mike: Noted. Any objections to adding a short followup test with only small models to isolate quantization/large-model effects?

ana: Good idea — mini A/B after primary run.

mike: OK scheduling note added. 02:00 UTC tomorrow. I'll create run thread with actual run ts when started. :rocket:

capacity-bot: [auto] test flagged: backpress-2303, run window 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z -> 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z, notify: #oncall, #prod-ops

sara: Thanks all.
